extracted.intended_audience: NAAIDC (NIAID) Council members, NIAID staff, NIH administrators, and grant applicants/administrators seeking to understand Council review procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Operating procedures governing how the NIAID National Advisory Allergy and Infectious Diseases Council (NAAIDC) reviews applications, concepts, and institute priorities, including rules for en bloc concurrence, special-consideration discussion, concept review outcomes, documentation, and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final review for scientific merit and program priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The NAAIDC provides final review, for scientific merit and program priority, of all applications for research grants, training grants, and career development awards assigned to the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, as well as other requests for support for which Council recommendations are required by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council evaluates both scientific merit and alignment with NIAID program priorities as the basis for recommendations to the NIH Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: En bloc concurrence eligibility (no special concerns)
rubrics_metrics.description: En bloc concurrence applies to applications for which the proposed project is relevant to the NIAID mission and shows promise of making valuable contributions to human knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before Council, three council members review an Electronic Council Book containing peer results and may recommend en bloc concurrence of peer review results for eligible applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unresolved concerns that preclude award without Council discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards will not be made for any applications with unresolved concerns (e.g., human subject, animal, biohazard, or inclusion concern identified by the study section).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any application with these unresolved issues must be discussed at Council rather than receiving en bloc concurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other issues requiring full Council discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Other issues that necessitate special consideration (e.g., foreign applications, unresolved appeal letters or other issue including MERIT award or extension requiring attention of full Council) will require that an application be discussed at the Council meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of special issues is not exclusive; any matter identified as needing attention must be brought to Council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for funding upon certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications with no special considerations will be eligible for funding as soon as the Council members have certified to the Executive Secretary of Council that their review is complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expedites funding decisions for streamlined (no-concern) applications once council certification occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual establishment of expedited review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Annually, Council establishes the criteria for expedited review and approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council sets and may revise the standards that determine which applications may be handled via expedited/en bloc processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics to be discussed in closed session (grants needing special consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: In closed session, Council (either in full or in Subcommittees) reviews grant applications, discussing topics such as selection of MERIT awardees and extensions, foreign grant applications, type 4 clinical extensions, inclusion of women and minorities and children in clinical studies, human subject or animal concerns, appeal letters, and concurrence with or variance from recommendations of initial review groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This list identifies specific substantive issues that trigger in-depth Council consideration and potential action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of applications from heavily funded PIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Council members and NIAID staff will review pending applications that are eligible for funding submitted by principal investigators who currently have a total of $2 million, or more, in total costs from NIH investigator-initiated grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications from PIs with high concurrent NIH funding receive explicit Council-level attention to funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to identify and flag applications for discussion or action
rubrics_metrics.description: Both Council members and NIAID staff may identify applications needing discussion or action. Council members may recommend deferral of applications with unresolved issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any member or staff can flag applications; flagged items may be deferred or brought for fuller consideration as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of streamlined (not discussed) applications with justification
rubrics_metrics.description: With appropriate justification and discussion, not discussed (streamlined) applications may be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even streamlined cases can be reopened for consideration if compelling reasons are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-meeting materials and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: An agenda, summary statements, special action work sheets, and other materials are provided to Council members approximately two weeks prior to meetings as background for these discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Council members are expected to review these materials in advance to inform discussion and voting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcommittee-to-full-Council recommendation process
rubrics_metrics.description: After the Subcommittees have met, their recommendations are brought to full Council for final consideration. Any Council member may raise an application for further discussion at the Subcommittee meeting or with full Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcommittees review and vet items first; full Council then makes final recommendations, with opportunity for any member to request further discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording and maintenance of Council recommendations and discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: NIAID staff will record all Council funding recommendations. NIAID staff will record and maintain documentation reflecting Subcommittee discussion and recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All decisions and deliberations relevant to funding and concepts must be documented and retained by staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept review outcomes for research initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: A Subcommittee may recommend approval, modification, deferral, or disapproval of a concept for a research initiative. Approved concepts are the bases for programs initiated through requests for applications, requests for proposals, and program announcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concepts originate from the scientific community, constituency organizations, and Congress; staff prepare concept summaries for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-session concept review process
rubrics_metrics.description: In open session, each Subcommittee conducts concept review of potential research initiatives using information from the scientific community, constituency organizations, and Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concept summaries prepared by NIAID staff are the basis for discussion; outcomes determine whether program solicitations will be developed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role in developing policy and research priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Council members serve as a national resource in the developing, recommending, and setting of Institute policy and research priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special working groups may be formed by or at the request of Council or NIAID to examine and address critical scientific or policy issues of importance to the Institute and its constituencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual intramural research program updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Annually, the Director of the Vaccine Research Center (VRC) shall provide an update on the intramural research program and the recommendations of VRC’s Board of Scientific Counselors and the Director of NIAID’s Division of Intramural Research (DIR) shall provide an update on the intramural research program and the recommendations of DIR’s Board of Scientific Counselors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These scheduled updates inform Council about intramural activities and external advisory recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIAID reporting obligations to Council
rubrics_metrics.description: NIAID will inform Council of current scientific, budgetary, legislative, or other issues that may have an impact on NIAID and its constituencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff must keep Council apprised of developments that could affect programmatic or funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Council of Councils representation and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: One member of the NAAIDC may serve as a member of the legislatively mandated NIH Council of Councils and report to the NAAIDC on the results of Council of Councils meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides linkage and information flow between NIH-wide advisory bodies and the NAAIDC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual review of Council Operating Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: At the first open session meeting of the calendar year, Council will review the Operating Procedures for the NAAIDC and make recommendations for revision, where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures are reviewed yearly and updated as needed to reflect current practice and policy.
